TITLE: the temporary start of noesar-debuglab modified its own container writable layer
ROOT_CAUSE: the analysis container writes python bytecode caches, semgrep settings and a detect-secrets temp file into its ephemeral upper layer whenever it runs; the phase-3 claim "no modification produced by its temporary start" was true of host data but over-broad at container-layer level
EVIDENCE: 25 files under the overlay2 upperdir carry mtimes inside the phase-3 window (06:27-07:29 UTC); its only writable bind mount, /mnt/cachec/NOESAR/debuglab/reports, has two files both dated 2026-07-09 and byte-identical before and after this phase
FIX: no code change: the deviation is inherent to running a scanner. The wording is corrected instead, here and in the phase-4 report
REGRESSION_TEST: re-hash of the writable bind mount before and after the phase-4 scan; 77 -> 77 files in the upper layer

TITLE: a TOTP code could be replayed within the acceptance window
ROOT_CAUSE: verifyTotp() checked only whether a code was arithmetically valid for the current +/-1 step; nothing recorded that a code had been spent, so a code observed once stayed usable for up to 90 seconds on a second, independent login. RFC 6238 section 5.2 forbids this
EVIDENCE: AUTH-19 reproduced it live before the fix: the same code that had just completed a login authenticated a second, separate session with HTTP 200
FIX: verifyTotpStep() reports the matching step; consumeTotp() refuses any step at or below the highest already accepted, persisted per user; applied to setup confirmation, login MFA and step-up reauthentication, each audited distinctly
REGRESSION_TEST: services/reference-control-plane/test/totp-replay.test.mjs, 8 tests including persistence across a restart and a check that a newer code is still accepted
STATUS: CLOSED - fixed, tested, AUTH-19 now PASS

TITLE: SSE stream aborted with no terminating error frame
ROOT_CAUSE: initial misdiagnosis: the abort was observed, but its cause was F4-004 killing the process, not a missing frame
EVIDENCE: the orchestrator unit test written to prove the defect passed immediately against unmodified code: an error inside the streaming try block does emit event: error and closes cleanly
FIX: none required
REGRESSION_TEST: stream-failure-containment.test.mjs test 2 keeps the property under guard
STATUS: WITHDRAWN - not a defect; recorded because it was reported before being verified

TITLE: one malformed chat request terminated the whole service
ROOT_CAUSE: POST /api/v1/chat/stream was invoked as `return orchestrator.streamToResponse(...)` without await, so a rejection escaped the handler try/catch and became an unhandled rejection, which Node turns into process exit. The orchestrator also wrote the SSE headers before validating the request, so the error could no longer be answered with a status. No process-level guard existed
EVIDENCE: three harness servers died with the identical stack (context-graph.mjs requiredText -> chat-orchestrator.mjs:60 -> server.mjs:592) on a request whose only fault was a missing `content` field; any session with provider.use could repeat it
FIX: await the call; move message validation and context building ahead of writeHead; make json() a no-op when headers are already sent; add process-level unhandledRejection (log and continue) and uncaughtException (log and exit for the supervisor) handlers
REGRESSION_TEST: stream-failure-containment.test.mjs (4) and stream-crash-survival.test.mjs (1), the latter driving a real child-process server and asserting it is still answering afterwards; verified to fail against the pre-fix files

TITLE: a reachable provider reported its health check as 500
ROOT_CAUSE: ProviderGateway.probe() built its success value from `providerId`, an identifier never declared in that scope (the parameter is profileId). In an ES module that is a ReferenceError, so only the failure path had ever worked
EVIDENCE: WORK-28 observed GET /api/v1/providers/{id}/health -> 500 with "providerId is not defined" in the log, while an unreachable provider returned a well-formed 502
FIX: providerId:profileId
REGRESSION_TEST: provider-health-probe.test.mjs, 3 tests covering healthy, upstream-error and disabled; verified to fail against the pre-fix file

TITLE: streaming chat never worked at all
ROOT_CAUSE: streamWithFallback() used the same undeclared `providerId` in `yield {providerId, delta}` and in its failure list, so a ReferenceError was thrown on the first delta of every stream and again when reporting why
EVIDENCE: every stream returned exactly two SSE frames, run then error, carrying "providerId is not defined"; after the fix the same request returns nine frames with real deltas
FIX: providerId:profileId in both places
REGRESSION_TEST: provider-gateway-success-paths.test.mjs, 9 tests driving every public gateway method to completion including fallback across a dead provider - the class existed because only failure paths had been executed

TITLE: a provider transport failure was reported as the single word "fetch failed"
ROOT_CAUSE: fetch() puts the real reason in error.cause; the gateway propagated only error.message, so a provider outage was undiagnosable from the audit trail
EVIDENCE: the SEC suite failures were opaque until cause reporting was added, at which point they read "UND_ERR_SOCKET other side closed" and became F4-009
FIX: describeFetchFailure() appends cause.code and cause.message
REGRESSION_TEST: covered indirectly by provider-gateway-success-paths.test.mjs; the stale-connection test asserts on behaviour rather than on the message

TITLE: two security-matrix rows described behaviour the code does not have
ROOT_CAUSE: row 12 cited tests/http-security.test.mjs as evidence for "CORS IMPLEMENTED", and that file contains no CORS test; row 33 claimed "user / project isolation IMPLEMENTED" while the reference-json data plane stores no per-user ownership on projects, conversations, memories, artifacts or sources
EVIDENCE: grep of http-security.test.mjs shows two tests, neither about CORS; grep of context-graph.mjs shows no ownerId/actorId/userId field anywhere; no route creates a second user, and the auth.manage permission is granted but wired to nothing
FIX: both rows rewritten to describe the real mechanism: CORS is enforced by the absence of any Access-Control-Allow-Origin grant plus SameSite=Strict cookies and a required CSRF header; isolation is per project, single-actor, with RLS existing only in the uninstalled Postgres schema
REGRESSION_TEST: SEC-04 asserts no CORS grant is ever emitted; WORK-13 and WORK-17 assert per-project isolation including vector search

TITLE: the first request after an idle pause could fail with an unexplained transport error
ROOT_CAUSE: undici reuses a pooled keep-alive socket that the upstream may already have closed, and does not retry a POST. Every provider closes idle connections, so a user-visible stream error could arise from a request that never reached the server
EVIDENCE: SEC-27 and SEC-30 failed reproducibly on "UND_ERR_SOCKET other side closed" while the same fixtures passed in isolation; an 8-second-idle probe did not reproduce it, which refuted the first hypothesis and led to the real one
FIX: fetchOnceRetryingStaleSocket() retries exactly once, only for stale-socket error codes, only when the request produced no bytes and the caller has not aborted
REGRESSION_TEST: provider-gateway-success-paths.test.mjs, "a connection the upstream has already closed is retried once", against a server with keepAliveTimeout=1ms
STATUS: CLOSED - fixed, tested, SEC-27 and SEC-30 now PASS

TITLE: provider and tool URL validation checks the hostname string, not the address reached
ROOT_CAUSE: validateBaseUrl() and endpoint() reject metadata literals and RFC1918 literals, but a hostname that resolves to an internal address passes; there is no resolve-then-check at connect time
EVIDENCE: SEC-15: registering https://internal.example.test/v1 as an external tool succeeds. Already disclosed in security matrix row 16 as a residual risk
FIX: NOT FIXED. A correct fix resolves the name and validates every returned address at connect time, which changes the transport layer and needs its own design; guessing at it inside an acceptance phase is how a partial mitigation becomes a false sense of safety
REGRESSION_TEST: SEC-15 records the limitation as PARTIAL rather than asserting a pass
STATUS: OPEN - accepted risk, recorded; exploitation requires provider.manage or agent.manage, i.e. owner or admin

TITLE: extraction is routed by filename extension and declared MIME type, with no content sniffing
ROOT_CAUSE: FileExtractor.extract() dispatches on the extension and the client-declared mimeType; magic bytes are never read
EVIDENCE: SEC-24: PDF bytes declared text/plain are stored as text; text declared application/pdf reaches pdftotext and fails extraction
FIX: NOT FIXED. This is a correctness limitation, not an execution risk: extractors run with shell:false on a temp path, output is capped, and nothing is ever executed. Adding sniffing changes ingestion behaviour for existing stored sources and belongs with the phase-5 documentation of supported formats
REGRESSION_TEST: SEC-24 records it as PARTIAL with the reasoning

TITLE: the declared 48 MiB ingestion limit cannot be reached through the JSON API
ROOT_CAUSE: uploads are base64-encoded in a JSON body, and 48 MiB inflates to exactly the 64 MiB request-body cap, so body() rejects first - and it rejects mid-upload, so the client sees a connection reset rather than a 413
EVIDENCE: SEC-19: a 46 MiB upload is accepted and capped at extraction; a 49 MiB upload resets the connection
FIX: none. Both limits are enforced; only the order and the surfaced error differ
REGRESSION_TEST: SEC-19 documents the interaction

TITLE: a full workspace backup is not encrypted and contains the auth master key
ROOT_CAUSE: the product exports user data without credentials (verified) but has no encrypted whole-workspace backup feature; a filesystem-level backup is an operator responsibility
EVIDENCE: the backup/restore evidence: 25/25 files restore byte-identical, credential files keep mode 0600 and hold binary key material, and conversation content is present in the clear in state/ai-workspace.json
FIX: none in this phase. Recorded so the phase-5 documentation states the operator duty explicitly rather than implying the product encrypts backups
REGRESSION_TEST: backup/restore verification records exactly what the archive contains

TITLE: migration 0012 could never be applied on any cluster
ROOT_CAUSE: it reshapes noesar_runtime.security_acceptance with CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW, inserting audit_hash_chain_guard before migration_ledger_immutable. PostgreSQL permits only APPENDING columns to a view, so the statement fails deterministically on every cluster that ran 0010 first, which is every cluster
EVIDENCE: the first real migration run stopped at 0012 with: cannot change name of view column "migration_ledger_immutable" to "audit_hash_chain_guard". This is direct evidence that the delivered migration set had never been executed against a real PostgreSQL, which is what B005=OPEN said
FIX: DROP VIEW IF EXISTS before CREATE VIEW, with the reason recorded in the migration itself; MIGRATIONS.json regenerated
REGRESSION_TEST: tools/acceptance/postgres-integration.mjs DB-06 and DB-07 apply all 16 migrations from an empty data directory and then re-apply, which fails against the pre-fix file

TITLE: a crashed database was never restarted, and the process reported success
ROOT_CAUSE: PostgresSupervisor scheduled its restart with setTimeout(...).unref(). An unref’d timer does not hold the event loop open, so when nothing else was pending Node drained the loop and exited with status 0 instead of restarting the cluster it had just watched die
EVIDENCE: the integration exercise ended at postgres.restart.scheduled and exited 0 with no further output, having printed no failure. In the server the HTTP listener keeps the loop alive, so the production path did restart - but the guarantee rested on an unrelated accident
FIX: the restart timer is no longer unref’d; the same applies to the socket and connection wait loops, where an early silent exit would have been equally invisible
REGRESSION_TEST: tools/acceptance/postgres-integration.mjs DB-30 SIGKILLs the postmaster and requires a NEW pid before passing, so a supervisor that never restarts fails rather than passing instantly

TITLE: no audit event could ever be appended to the PostgreSQL ledger
ROOT_CAUSE: migration 0007 enabled and FORCED row level security on noesar_audit.events and gave it a policy FOR SELECT only. With FORCE and no INSERT policy every append is denied, so PostgresRepository.appendAuditEvent() could not have written a row
EVIDENCE: an INSERT through the application role was refused by RLS before the fix; grep of 0007 shows the single policy is FOR SELECT
FIX: migration 0015 adds an INSERT policy requiring workspace membership and actor identity; UPDATE and DELETE remain unreachable, which is what the immutability trigger is for
REGRESSION_TEST: postgres-integration.mjs DB-41 appends an event as the application role, DB-42 asserts it cannot be deleted

TITLE: accounts were created that could never log in
ROOT_CAUSE: AuthService.completeLogin() decrypts user.totp unconditionally. Until multi-user existed there was exactly one account and it always had a TOTP secret, so the assumption held. The new invitation flow created ordinary users without one, and every login attempt would have dereferenced null
EVIDENCE: found by end-to-end testing against a live server, not by any unit test: an invited user reached the MFA step of login with no envelope to decrypt. No unit test covered it because the fixtures always bootstrapped an owner
FIX: every INTERACTIVE account now enrols MFA before it exists - stronger than the requirement, which names only owner and admin. The alternative was a login branch that issues a session after the password step alone, and a code path that can skip a factor is a code path that can be reached by mistake. completeLogin also refuses a credential-less account explicitly (403, audited) instead of throwing
REGRESSION_TEST: test/user-directory.test.mjs "every interactive account enrols MFA, not only the privileged roles" and "a service account is created without any MFA enrolment"; multi-user-isolation.mjs MU-08b performs a real password+TOTP login as an ordinary user

TITLE: an invitation token stayed usable while MFA enrolment was in flight
ROOT_CAUSE: the invitation was marked accepted only when enrolment completed, so between accept and confirm the token could start a second, parallel enrolment with a different password - last confirmation wins
EVIDENCE: reproduced directly: two acceptInvitation calls with the same token both succeeded before the fix
FIX: the invitation is consumed when it is CLAIMED. The claim lapses with the enrolment window so a fumbled authenticator setup is recoverable rather than permanently locking the invitation
REGRESSION_TEST: test/user-directory.test.mjs "an invitation cannot be replayed, revoked-then-used, or used after expiry" and "an invitation claim lapses with the enrolment window so a fumbled setup is recoverable"

TITLE: the Phase 4 remediation left two copies of provider-gateway.mjs calling a function that does not exist
ROOT_CAUSE: commit 04878c4 applied the F4-006/F4-007/F4-009 fixes to the shipped copy in full and to ai-workspace/provider-gateway.mjs and ai-workspace/runtime/provider-gateway.mjs partially: the call sites were renamed to fetchOnceRetryingStaleSocket, the helper definitions were never added. This is the same defect class F4-005 and F4-006 were, reintroduced by their own fix
EVIDENCE: git show 0a434eb proves all three copies were byte-identical (a07d385b...) at the end of Phase 3. ESLint reported six no-undef errors across the two copies on its very first run. Neither file is shipped - the Dockerfile copies only services/reference-control-plane/ - so no release was affected
FIX: three-way identity restored from the corrected shipped copy; all three now hash to 9e3bd86f...
REGRESSION_TEST: tools/run-eslint.sh over the whole repository, with no-undef as an error and no file exempt; tools/verify-linter-detects.sh proves the detector fires on this exact shape

TITLE: a blanket privilege grant silently undid the audit ledger revoke
ROOT_CAUSE: a draft of the supervisor issued GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA ... TO noesar_app after every migration run, which re-granted the DELETE on noesar_audit.events that migration 0009 deliberately revokes
EVIDENCE: caught while wiring the first successful migration run; the grant ran after 0009 and therefore always won
FIX: the blanket grant was removed entirely and privileges moved into migration 0016, where they are reviewable as a diff. Privileges expressed in a loop cannot be
REGRESSION_TEST: postgres-integration.mjs DB-42 (append-only enforced) and DB-08b (the application role cannot write the migration ledger)

TITLE: the Phase 4 inventory said the image has zero third-party npm dependencies; syft finds 199
ROOT_CAUSE: both are right about different things. The PRODUCT declares no dependency; the IMAGE ships npm and yarn from the base image, and npm carries 197 bundled packages under /usr/local/lib/node_modules
EVIDENCE: syft 1.49.0 image scan, grouped by location: 197 under /usr/local/lib/node_modules, 1 /opt/noesar/package.json, 1 /opt/yarn-v1.22.22/package.json
FIX: no code change. SBOM_REPORT.md states both numbers and what each measures, because a vulnerability matcher run against this image will report on the bundled tree and be correct to
REGRESSION_TEST: the SBOM itself is the evidence; tools/generate-sbom.sh regenerates it from a pinned tool and image

TITLE: the log redactor corrupted 6.75% of all UUIDs, including correlation and incident identifiers
ROOT_CAUSE: the phone rule /(?<!\w)(?:\+?\d[\d .()-]{7,}\d)(?!\w)/ matches inside a canonical UUID - "...-2822-4650-..." is nine characters of digits and hyphens - and rewrote the middle of it as [REDACTED_PHONE]. Every string value in every log record passes through redactText
EVIDENCE: measured: 13497 of 200000 randomUUID() values altered, 6.75%. This is the root cause of the flake Phase 4 observed once and could not reproduce; the stress harness reproduced it twice in 270 runs, once breaking "a trace record carries its incident id and scope" and once also breaking "every response carries a correlation id the operator can search on". Phase 4 had attributed it to timing races in two unrelated files
FIX: canonical UUIDs are lifted out before any rule runs and restored afterwards. A UUID is an identifier, never a phone number or a payment card, and partially rewriting one destroys the correlation the identifier exists to provide
REGRESSION_TEST: test/redaction-identifier-integrity.test.mjs, 9 tests including 20000 random UUIDs and 300 correlation ids written through the real Logger; 7 of the 9 fail against the pre-fix module

TITLE: an IPv4 address was redacted under the label [REDACTED_PHONE]
ROOT_CAUSE: rule order: the phone rule also matches "192.168.1.7" and ran before the ipv4 rule, so the address was protected but mislabelled - contradicting the Phase 3 logging note, which states IPv4 literals become [REDACTED_IP]
EVIDENCE: redactText("192.168.1.7") returned "[REDACTED_PHONE]" before the fix
FIX: the ipv4 rule now runs before the phone rule. The data was protected either way; the label was a lie, and a label nobody can trust is a label nobody reads
REGRESSION_TEST: test/redaction-identifier-integrity.test.mjs "an IPv4 address is labelled as an address, not as a phone number", which also asserts a dotted phone number is still a phone number

TITLE: the UUID placeholder introduced by the F4C-009 fix could be forged from attacker-controlled text
ROOT_CAUSE: the placeholder is NUL-delimited, and a JSON string may carry a literal U+0000. Text containing one could forge a placeholder and be substituted with a UUID lifted from elsewhere in the same value, or with the string "undefined" when the index was out of range
EVIDENCE: found by probing the fix rather than by a test that expected it: a crafted input returned "undefined", and another returned a real identifier belonging to a different part of the same string
FIX: U+0000 is stripped from the input before tokenisation, so after that point no NUL exists in the text except the ones this function inserted. A control character has no business in a log line in any case
REGRESSION_TEST: test/redaction-identifier-integrity.test.mjs "a placeholder cannot be forged from user-supplied text", covering the plain, forged and out-of-range cases

TITLE: a TOTP regression test depended on the wall clock not crossing a step boundary
ROOT_CAUSE: the test generates a code, runs a login, then asserts the previous step’s code is still arithmetically valid. verifyTotp re-samples Date.now(), so if the clock crossed a 30-second boundary mid-test the code became two steps old, outside the +/-1 window, and the assertion failed for a reason the test was never about
EVIDENCE: reproduced by tools/flake-stress.mjs: 1 failure in 50 isolated runs of totp-replay.test.mjs, with the signature "the older code is still arithmetically valid, which is the point". This is the second of the two candidates Phase 4 named
FIX: the test anchors itself inside a step with at least 10 seconds of headroom before starting, and verifies against that anchor instead of re-sampling the clock. Fails closed either way - a spurious failure, never a spurious pass
REGRESSION_TEST: the test itself, plus tools/flake-stress.mjs which is now a committed tool rather than a one-off

TITLE: the postgres.ready log line reports migrations=0 on a restart of a fully migrated cluster
ROOT_CAUSE: the field counts migrations applied BY THAT START, which is correctly zero when all 16 are already applied. The data-plane.ready line emitted immediately afterwards reports the true total of 16
EVIDENCE: observed across a real docker restart of the installed container: postgres.ready migrations=0 followed by data-plane.ready migrations=16
FIX: NOT FIXED. Renaming the field means rebuilding and reinstalling the image for a log label, and the adjacent line already carries the unambiguous number. Recorded so a future reader is not misled into thinking the schema is missing
REGRESSION_TEST: none; the behaviour is documented in POSTGRESQL_18_PGVECTOR_IMPLEMENTATION.md under stated limits

TITLE: the Phase 4 handoff gives a setup-token fingerprint that does not match the installation
ROOT_CAUSE: the handoff and BACKUP_RESTORE_TEST_REPORT.md both record af6f7ca93c31 as the first-owner setup token fingerprint of the real installation. The value most likely came from the throwaway probe container Phase 4 used for the bootstrap rehearsal, which had its own workspace and therefore its own token
EVIDENCE: the Phase 4 container itself logged setup_fingerprint=db1cf03ef221 at 12:20:43 on its own startup, before any work in this gate; the phase4-complete container logs the same value at 14:23 and 14:25; and the product own fingerprint() over the file on disk returns db1cf03ef221. So the recorded value did not match even when it was written
FIX: the handoff now records db1cf03ef221 AND tells the Owner to verify against the setup-token.available line in the live container log rather than against any transcribed value, because the token rotates on expiry and a fingerprint in a document goes stale by design
REGRESSION_TEST: none automated. The correct value is emitted by the runtime on every start, which is the source the handoff now points at

TITLE: unauthenticated /metrics is gated on the peer being a private address, a premise LAN publishing invalidates
ROOT_CAUSE: the gate was if(!isInternalAddress(clientIp(req))), justified by a code comment stating the container publishes on loopback only. Behind a published Docker port every external caller arrives from the bridge gateway (172.22.0.1), itself RFC1918, so the predicate returns internal for a LAN browser exactly as readily as for a host-local process. Harmless while the publish is loopback because nothing else can reach the port; false the moment it is not
EVIDENCE: executed rather than read: over the LAN address GET /metrics returned 200 with 28 series before the fix and 401 after. The disclosure is request paths, status codes per route, safe-mode state, log byte count and a latency histogram - no credentials and no user content
FIX: exposure scope made an explicit declared input (NOESAR_BIND_ADDRESS / NOESAR_BIND_SCOPE) instead of an assumption in a comment; unauthenticated /metrics now requires scope=loopback AND a private peer. The address predicate was kept, moved to http-security.mjs and unit-tested, because it is a correct statement about an address - what was wrong was the conclusion drawn from it without knowing the exposure
REGRESSION_TEST: services/reference-control-plane/test/lan-exposure.test.mjs - 11 checks including a positive assertion that loopback installations still get 200, so the fix cannot be mistaken for a blanket lockdown. Verified to FAIL against the pre-fix predicate before being trusted

TITLE: PROJECT_STATE.json recorded an image ID the installation was not running
ROOT_CAUSE: the state file was written before the image was rebuilt. It named sha256:ec2ac8bd; the tag noesar-evolution:phase4-complete was moved to sha256:52987fbb at 14:22 UTC and the container created from that at 14:23
EVIDENCE: docker inspect of the running container reports Image=sha256:52987fbb; docker image inspect sha256:ec2ac8bd succeeds but returns RepoTags=[] - the digest still exists, untagged. Every enumerated precondition of this gate (tag, container, bind, port, health, clean tree) nonetheless matched
FIX: PROJECT_STATE.json corrected, and the superseded value recorded in PHASE_4_COMPLETION_REPORT.md rather than silently overwritten
REGRESSION_TEST: none automated. A digest recorded by hand goes stale by construction; the durable fix is to read it from docker inspect, which the reproduction commands now do

TITLE: the installers readiness loop always probed 127.0.0.1 regardless of where the port was published
ROOT_CAUSE: both Unraid installers polled http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/healthz to decide whether the container had started. With NOESAR_BIND_ADDRESS set to a LAN address, loopback does not answer at all
EVIDENCE: the loop runs 30 attempts and then prints INSTALLATION_STARTUP=FAIL. A LAN install would have reported failure for a container that was healthy, and the operator response - tear it down and retry - would have been provoked by the check rather than by the product
FIX: a probe address is derived from the bind address (loopback only when the publish is a wildcard) and used in the readiness loop; the final URL is printed with the published address
REGRESSION_TEST: tools/test-installer-hardening.mjs asserts the probe targets the published address AND does not fall back to loopback - both directions, because only asserting the first would pass on a script that probed both

TITLE: a LAN publish would have answered 421 to every browser request
ROOT_CAUSE: NOESAR_ALLOWED_HOSTS is baked into the image as localhost,127.0.0.1,::1. A browser opening http://192.168.178.100:8100/ sends Host: 192.168.178.100:8100, which is not in that set
EVIDENCE: verified live before the change: curl -H Host: 192.168.178.100:8100 against the loopback publish returned 421 Unrecognized Host header. Correct behaviour, and fatal for the objective of this gate
FIX: the runtime adds NOESAR_BIND_ADDRESS to the allowlist itself, and the installers derive the allowlist entry from the same setting that drives the publish, so the two cannot drift apart. Only the declared address is added, never its subnet
REGRESSION_TEST: lan-exposure.test.mjs asserts the declared address is accepted and 192.168.178.101, attacker.example are both still 421. Written first with fetch(), which silently drops a Host header - see the report; rewritten with node:http plus a negative control

TITLE: deployment/docker/run.sh hardcoded 127.0.0.1 in the publish
ROOT_CAUSE: the script had no bind variable at all, so there was no supported way to reach it from another machine - the operator would have had to edit the script
EVIDENCE: read directly: --publish "127.0.0.1:${PORT}:8088" with no indirection, while the two Unraid installers already honoured NOESAR_BIND_ADDRESS
FIX: the same access-mode decision as the other two installers, through the shared deployment/lib/network-access.sh, with the same loopback default
REGRESSION_TEST: tools/test-installer-hardening.mjs runs all three installers through every access-mode scenario

TITLE: the wrong setup-token fingerprint af6f7ca93c31 survived in two documents after F4C-014 was closed
ROOT_CAUSE: F4C-014 corrected the handoff but left PHASE_4_COMPLETION_REPORT.md and BACKUP_RESTORE_TEST_REPORT.md, where the value was still presented as this installation fingerprint
EVIDENCE: grep across docs/ found four occurrences: two corrective (the handoff note and the finding register) and two asserting it as fact. The real value is db1cf03ef221, confirmed from the file on disk and the live container log in this gate
FIX: BACKUP_RESTORE_TEST_REPORT.md corrected with a note explaining what the value was and why the equality it demonstrates is unaffected. The completion report occurrence describes the defect and is left, because erasing it would erase the finding
REGRESSION_TEST: none automated. Both documents now tell the reader to verify against the setup-token.available line in the live log, never against a transcribed value, because the token rotates on expiry

TITLE: --memory-swap is accepted by the daemon and silently discarded by this kernel
ROOT_CAUSE: the host runs cgroup v2 without swap accounting; /proc/swaps is empty and there is no memory.swap.max at the cgroup root
EVIDENCE: docker run printed WARNING: Your kernel does not support swap limit capabilities or the cgroup is not mounted, and HostConfig.MemorySwap reads -1 in the resulting container despite --memory-swap 8g being passed
FIX: NOT FIXED - there is nothing to fix in this product. The flag is passed by all three installers because it is correct on a host that supports it; on this host it is inert and the intended outcome holds anyway since there is no swap to spill into
REGRESSION_TEST: none. Recorded so a reader does not conclude from the flag list that swap is bounded here. CONTAINER_SECURITY_PROFILE.md states it too
